motions.item_title: Appoint Emily Buss to the Library Advisory Board, completing a three-year term through December…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to appoint Emily Buss to the Library Advisory Board, completing a three-year term through December 2027. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Emily Buss joins the Library Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Emily Buss to the Library Advisory Board, finishing out a three-year term that runs through December 2027.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day at the library — this fills one seat on the board that advises the city on library matters.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda, moving items 13.A. January 7, 2025 Minutes, and 13.B. January 21, 2025 Minutes to a future Council meeting agenda, and moving 12.A. Firefly 4MG Tank Change Order #2, and 14.C. A Resolution Consenting to the Annexation of 178 Acres of Land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District to the Scheduled Items for further discussion. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, four items pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda while pushing two sets of minutes to a later meeting and moving two other items to full discussion.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this only decides which items get talked through and which wait for a future meeting.

motions.item_title: Approve Change Order #2 for the Firefly 4MG Tank in the amount of $189,985.67
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve Change Order #2 for the Firefly 4MG Tank in the amount of $189,985.67. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: $190K more for the Firefly water tank
motions.summary: The council took up a change order adding $189,985.67 to the cost of the Firefly 4-million-gallon water tank.
motions.impact: This adds money to a city water storage tank already under contract. The motion sets no change to your water bill, and the record does not show a final outcome.

motions.item_title: A Resolution Consenting to the Annexation of 178 Acres of Land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution Consenting to the Annexation of 178 Acres of Land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: 178 acres proposed for Pole Canyon district
motions.summary: The council took up a resolution consenting to the annexation of 178 acres of land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District.
motions.impact: This concerns the 178 acres in question and which district serves them, not existing neighborhoods. The meeting record does not show how this one ended.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City backs an inland port project area
motions.summary: The council formally supported creating a Utah Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain, a development designation created under state law.
motions.impact: This is the city's show of support, not the final word — the state port authority decides whether the project area happens. Nothing changes on the ground yet.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Meadow Ranch Plat 4, Lot 433
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Meadow Ranch Plat 4, Lot 433. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: One lot rezoned in Meadow Ranch
motions.summary: The council approved a zoning change for a single property, Lot 433 in Meadow Ranch Plat 4.
motions.impact: This affects one lot and its immediate neighbors, not the wider city. The motion does not say what the new zoning allows, so check with the city if you live nearby.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Amended Plat for Saddle Junction Plat 1 (Allgood Plat Amendment)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Amended Plat for Saddle Junction Plat 1 (Allgood Plat Amendment). Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Lot lines redrawn at Saddle Junction
motions.summary: The council approved an amended plat for Saddle Junction Plat 1, known as the Allgood plat amendment.
motions.impact: This touches only the property involved. A plat amendment is the paperwork that adjusts how a parcel is drawn on the official map — nothing changes for other residents.

motions.item_title: Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezone for Spring Run Plaza
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to TABLE the Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezone for Spring Run Plaza. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Spring Run Plaza decision delayed
motions.summary: The council set aside the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza instead of voting it up or down.
motions.impact: If you live near the proposed Spring Run Plaza, nothing is settled — the plan and the zoning change are still open and can come back to the council later.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood set an end time of 11:00 PM for the meeting. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Meeting capped at 11 p.m.
motions.summary: The council agreed to end the night's meeting at 11:00 p.m.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is housekeeping the council uses to limit how late the meeting runs.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.60.120 General Fencing and Screening Provisions as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.60.120 General Fencing and Screening Provisions as presented. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a majority vote of 4:1.
motions.headline: New rules for fences and screening
motions.summary: The council rewrote the section of city code covering general fencing and screening, changing the rules that apply when property owners put up a fence or wall.
motions.impact: If you are planning a fence at your home or business, check the updated code before you build — the requirements are not the same as they were.

motions.item_title: Adopt an Ordinance Partially Suspending the Collection of the Transportation Impact Fee for Non…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance Partially Suspending the Collection of the Transportation Impact Fee for Nonresidential Developments with the changes of removing the restaurant exception from all building sizes. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Impact fee cut for new businesses
motions.summary: The city partially suspended its transportation impact fee for nonresidential development, and dropped the carve-out that had applied to restaurants at every building size.
motions.impact: If you are building a business, store, or office in Eagle Mountain, you will pay less in road impact fees. The restaurant carve-out no longer applies at any size.

motions.item_title: Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fifth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fifth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget as presented. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mid-year budget update approved
motions.summary: The council approved the fifth amendment to the city's 2024-2025 budget, adjusting the spending plan partway through the fiscal year.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the bookkeeping the city does to keep its budget lined up with actual spending. No dollar figures were stated in the motion.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting an Amended Water Conservation and Management Plan for Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting an Amended Water Conservation and Management Plan for Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Updated water conservation plan adopted
motions.summary: The city adopted an amended water conservation and management plan, the document that sets out how Eagle Mountain manages and conserves its water supply.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this adopts a planning document. The council did not set any new watering rules or restrictions with this vote.
